Miguel (Sales): FYI vendor-risk just pinged about our SIG answers. They want a crisp section on encryption & KMS for their review. Can we put together a short canonical reply that I can paste into their portal?
Aisha (Security): Sure. High-level bullets first: at-rest: AES-256-GCM envelope encryption; in-transit: TLS 1.3 with forward secrecy. Key hierarchy: customer data encrypted with DEKs; DEKs wrapped by CMKs.
Ravi (Solutions): Add deployment modes: Hosted (Redwood-managed KMS), BYOK with cloud KMS (AWS/GCP/Azure), and Private with HSM (PKCS#11 or CloudHSM). Note we also support multi-account key references for enterprise isolation.
Miguel (Sales): They specifically asked if we ever handle plaintext customer keys and whether keys leave HSM boundaries.
Aisha (Security): We never persist plaintext CMKs. For BYOK we store only the key identifier/ARN and call the customer's KMS for cryptographic ops. For HSM-backed keys (CloudHSM or on-prem HSM), key material never leaves the HSM; operations happen inside the crypto boundary.
Ravi (Solutions): Example for the questionnaire: "We support customer-managed keys via AWS KMS, GCP KMS, and Azure Key Vault. For on-prem or FIPS workloads we integrate with customer HSMs using PKCS#11; private deployments can be configured so key material never leaves customer infrastructure."
Miguel (Sales): Nice. Rotation and re-encryption? They want to know if rotation causes downtime or data re-encryption costs.
Aisha (Security): Rotation model: DEKs are rotated regularly and per-tenant; CMKs can use KMS-native automatic rotation or customer-triggered rotation. Because we use envelope encryption, rotating the CMK does not force immediate re-encryption of existing ciphertexts; new DEKs are wrapped with the new CMK. We offer an explicit rewrap job for customers who want full re-encryption (scheduled, offline). Typical guidance: CMK rotation cadence 90d for high-security, 365d standard.
Ravi (Solutions): For the POC we can show a rewrap runbook with estimated throughput: e.g., ~500 GB/hr on a 4-GPU Dedicated pool with default IO patterns (approx). We’ll caveat with model cache hotness and network egress.
Miguel (Sales): Can we provide a short snippet showing how to grant Redwood permission to use a customer CMK in AWS?
Ravi (Solutions): Yes, include the AWS create-grant example:
```bash
aws kms create-grant --key-id $CMK_ARN --grantee-principal arn:aws:iam::redwood:role/service --operations Encrypt Decrypt GenerateDataKey --name "redwood-grant"
```
Aisha (Security): Add auditability: all key operations (GenerateDataKey, Encrypt, Decrypt, ReEncrypt, DescribeKey) are logged. Hosted customers can have KMS logs forwarded to their S3/Syslog/SIEM. Private deployments integrate with local audit pipelines.
Miguel (Sales): They also asked about compromise procedures and SLAs for key APIs.
Aisha (Security): Incident procedure: immediate revocation/rotation, start investigation playbook, provide full operation audit and timeline, optional rewrap. For SLA: Dedicated/Private customers can contract availability and response SLAs for key management APIs; hosted customers get operational SLAs documented in our plan pages.
Infra Bot: Created ticket #5098 to track vendor-risk SIG follow-up and attach example configs. ETA 3 business days.
Ravi (Solutions): Suggest we send a 1-page answer plus an annex with CLI examples and a short rewrap performance table. I’ll draft the annex.
Miguel (Sales): Great — I'll paste the bullets into their portal and schedule a quick call with Aisha and Ravi. Thanks team. :thumbsup:
Aisha (Security): One more minor clarification: we use AES-256-GCM for DEKs and endorse TLS 1.3 (AEAD ciphers) for network transport. Mention FIPS-validated HSMs supported for compliance customers.
Ravi (Solutions): I'll attach an appendix listing supported providers and a sample BYOK YAML for private deployments.
Miguel (Sales): Sending now.
